allow.reason: Spec v3 3.4 row 1: the brand definition is the one place an id is a string; every id type is built from it.
Generic over every id: K is the record's own key type (RoomId, LampId, ...), so its bound is string.

D1: ofId is keyed by the registry's own entity or device id. Its readers look up lists that mix lamps, bulbs, on/off lights and switches (a switch range can be set on an on/off light), so no one id kind fits until those lists are split (V3).

D3: each case's payload is the text the scripts join into the saved key: a block's scope (a room, or house, joined as Jinja `~` joins any value), a remote's source id, a dashboard control's light and scope suffix, a native control's base (`room:<room>` or a lamp), and a saved key of no known shape, kept unread (spec 3.4 row 5). They narrow to ids as their producers are typed.
D3: the overlay key's saved text, the wire form at the save edge.
A sort comparator's result.
Spec v3 3.4 row 1: the range definition is the one place a range type is a number; every range type is built from it.
Spec v3 3.4 row 1: the range mark's name parameter, the same mark on a range that is not a number.

V1 room site, kept: this is `Rooms.ofId`, the registry's entity-or-device -> room map. Its keys are the registry's own ids and mix lamps, bulbs, on/off lights and switches, so no one id kind fits them (the `Rooms` entry's reason); its values are already RoomIds.

V1 switch site, kept: the cache fingerprint's on/off list as observed, `labelled(view, 'on_off')` (label members, device-expanded in the domain) plus the saved switch-range keys, compared with the stored fingerprint as text. The schedule plans the same `on_off` entities as lamps, so they are not all switches; branding the list needs the label list split and parsed at the snapshot edge (V3).
